page.title: Publications
page.intro: ISRD publishes working papers, research reports, and methodology notes documenting our systemic synthesis approach and its application across research programs. All publications are grounded in interactive simulation and AI-assisted analysis.
page.status_note: Publications marked 'In Preparation' are active working papers. Those marked 'Forthcoming' are near completion. All are available for early review on request.

publications.title: Systemic Synthesis as a Research Framework: Attractor-Based Modelling Across Domains
publications.abstract: Presents the foundational methodology of Systemic Synthesis — a non-linear, attractor-based approach to modelling complex adaptive systems. Describes the Sim-Toolkit architecture, the feedback graph primitive, and the principles governing multi-domain application. Argues for a shift from reductionist systems analysis toward engineering that accounts for basin dynamics, bifurcation thresholds, and emergent stability.

publications.title: Post-Viral ME/CFS as a Brainstem Attractor State: A Population Simulation Model
publications.abstract: Presents a 100-person agent-based simulation of viral outbreak and ME/CFS conversion, calibrated against published epidemiological benchmarks (Wessely et al. 1995; Jason et al.; Carruthers et al. 2011; Chicago mono study). Models the brainstem-HPA axis as a structural attractor that, once destabilised by viral insult in susceptible individuals, resists return to healthy function. Identifies autonomic involvement during acute illness as the strongest single predictor of ME/CFS conversion.

publications.title: Narrative as Feedback System: A Reader-First Framework for Systemic Writing
publications.abstract: Proposes that effective narrative structure can be modelled as a directed feedback graph in which reader clarity, tension, and engagement are interdependent stock-and-flow variables. Introduces the Reader-First Systemic Writing framework, applies attractor theory to reader drop-off and emotional arc, and demonstrates how small structural interventions can cascade through the narrative system. AI-assisted structural analysis is used to map passages to feedback graph nodes.

publications.title: Civilisational Tipping Points: Socio-Economic Attractor Basins in the 21st Century
publications.abstract: Models civilisational stability as a multi-basin attractor landscape with at least four identifiable equilibrium states: stable cooperation, managed tension, rising disorder, and systemic collapse. Using a five-node feedback simulation calibrated to contemporary socio-economic data, we identify inequality and social infrastructure degradation as the highest-leverage tipping variables. AI-assisted scenario generation is used to explore rare but high-impact bifurcation events.
